clue.text: One handing out punishment is more decent going round island

indicators.note: going round means wrapping about something, so one word sits inside the other

blocks.note: chaste means pure or decent; this is its comparative

explanation.surface: A disciplinarian is described as morally upright while travelling around an island.
explanation.definitionFit: To chastise is to punish or rebuke, so a chastiser is the person who metes out that punishment.

clue.text: Amusing play without denouement pertaining to oneself is a a source of disappointment

your own things belong to yourself

explanation.surface: A comic play with no proper ending, about its own author, lets the audience down.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed clue repeats 'a' ('is a a source'); the duplicate is a typo and plays no part.
explanation.definitionFit: A comedown is a fall in status or an anticlimax, something that disappoints.

clue.text: A model upset fabulist

blocks.note: taken as written
to model is to pose

explanation.definitionFit: Aesop is the ancient Greek storyteller famed for his fables, the archetypal fabulist.

clue.text: Novel arrangement of undersea trials?

explanation.definitionFit: Treasure Island is Robert Louis Stevenson's 1883 adventure novel about pirates and buried gold.

the first letter of teetotal

explanation.definitionFit: Stealth is secret, sly action, so as a noun it matches cunning in the sense of craftiness.

explanation.definitionFit: To resume is to begin again after a pause, matching the third-person verb form.

clue.text: To start with, try on girlfriend's sexy clothes!

the first letter of surveillance

clue.text: Ordinary places where grass might grow

explanation.walkthrough: A common is a patch of open public grassland in British villages; read word for word, the phrase names two grassy spots.
explanation.definitionFit: Common-or-garden is a British idiom for something ordinary, everyday, nothing special.

clue.text: Author Kate taking supermodel to Europe

clue.text: Settled comfortably in newly built den, consuming calorie-laden cake

a scone is a small plain cake
C is the abbreviation for calorie

explanation.surface: Someone has made themselves at home in a new den, eating fattening cake.
explanation.walkthrough: There are two insertions, one inside the other: the calorie goes into the cake first, and that whole cake then goes into the rebuilt den.
explanation.definitionFit: To be ensconced is to have settled oneself snugly and securely in a place.

clue.text: Corrupt, so plead for removal from high office

embers are the glowing remnants of a fire

taken as written

clue.text: Reprimanded and marked as having been done

blocks.note: first meaning: told off sharply
second meaning: checked off a list

explanation.walkthrough: Both senses are past participles, so each swaps neatly for the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Ticked off is informal for scolded, and literally describes items given a tick on a list once completed.

clue.text: Worried by puddings rising

clue.text: German replacing head of KGB in Russian government structure is a source of trouble

taken as written

clue.text: Drugs scored from sweet member of the upper classes
